requirement: Implement SecureAsyncLCELPipeline that prevents PromptTemplate injection and executes async LCEL chains without blocking the asyncio event loop. User inputs must be safely encapsulated as human messages without evaluating curly braces {} as template formatting keys. Sync heavy preprocessing must be offloaded via asyncio.to_thread. The pipeline's astream() method must yield token chunks incrementally.
skeleton: Secure prompt formatter and async LCEL pipeline with non-blocking offload and streaming.

rationale.teaches: A pipeline that keeps user input in its own human message, strips role delimiters in strict mode, offloads sync work with asyncio.to_thread, and streams tokens incrementally.
rationale.why: Injection succeeds only when user text is concatenated into the system role, and blocking shows only under a concurrent task. The fixture injects a fake System: line and times a concurrent coroutine during the sync step.

candidates.why_wrong: User input is concatenated into the system message, so a user can rewrite the system instruction.
Role delimiters are not stripped, so a user message containing a System: line is passed through.
The sync digest runs on the event loop, so concurrent coroutines stall while it computes.
All tokens are accumulated and yielded once, so the caller sees nothing until the stream ends.
strict_sanitization defaults to False, so the default pipeline passes injected delimiters through.
